description: Legacy Recon is local, read-only static recon at the NARROWED OBSERVED SCOPE in CLAIM-SCOPE.md: point an agent at a directory and get (a) an architecture map (languages, packages, entry points, layering signals, file/size distribution), (b) a scoped dependency + end-of-life risk list (the README-listed manifest parsers plus a small explicit versioned-in-code EOL rules table; each EOL entry cites its rule id), and (c) modernization estimate INPUTS — LOC by language, test presence/ratio, manifest age signals, coupling hotspots by fan-in — raw inputs, never an estimate. Novel mechanism: evidence-bound recon at the NARROWED OBSERVED SCOPE (CLAIM-SCOPE.md). Positive DECLARED, OBSERVED, and INFERRED reports only within CLAIM-SCOPE.md, with evidence or basis carried in the output; OBSERVED is not exhaustive. Within that scope, reported entries cite a file path plus the manifest line, structural fact, or inference basis they rest on; standing UNKNOWN categories carry reasons, never a guessed stack; DECLARED (manifest), OBSERVED (import statements), and INFERRED (labeled inference with basis) stay in separate lists. OBSERVED is a scoped positive inventory, not an exhaustive or universal JS/TS claim. Withdrawn by name: W1 JS/TS multiline block-comment continuation after a split no-closing-slash span; W2 chained no-closing-slash JS/TS spans on one line; W3 B-LR-14 invalid-line identifier-follow shapes; W4 exhaustive OBSERVED recall; W5 dynamic-import observation or a dedicated dynamic-import UNKNOWN; W6 .mts/.cts OBSERVED extraction; W7 completeness over permission-denied subtrees; W8 report-and-skip treatment of self-referential symlink loops; W9 hosted, authenticated, or multi-tenant operation. Safety: target code is never executed or imported, ordinary symlinks are never traversed (resolvable escapes are reported), binary and oversize files are skipped and counted, and the file-count cap surfaces as a named truncation flag. Free, services-led: a narrowed-scope recon can be a qualified modernization lead for CETech's legacy modernization line.
